correctness.rationale: Fix n>=3, fair independent edges of labeled K_n and feasible even-weight binary degree syndrome d. Its binary incidence matrix has rank n-1, so every parity fiber has 2^(M-n+1) graphs, M=C(n,2). Apply character expansion of 1_{Bx=d} and independent edge products to obtain Z=(1+i)^M/2^(M+1)*sum_{k=0}^n K_k(w;n)(-i)^{k(n-k)}, where K_k are coefficients of (1-t)^w(1+t)^(n-w). For even n, the k-phase takes only its even/odd constants; F(1)=F(-1)=0 for 0<w<n, while w=0 or n gives explicit nonzero endpoints. For odd n the trigonometric roots of unity and even w evaluate to the stated nonzero phase and magnitude. Symmetric difference with any fixed triangle on >=3 vertices preserves every degree parity but reverses parity of E, so conditional E[(-1)^E]=0; four-root inversion gives P(E≡a mod4|D=d)=[1+2 Re(i^(-a) Z)]/4 and uniformity iff Z=0. Independently enumerated all graphs on n=3,4,5,6 and verified all 4 residue counts and characteristic-function closed forms for every feasible syndrome, total 8+64+1024+32768=33864 graphs. The all-order argument uses exact algebra and the triangle involution, not exhaustive finite extrapolation.
residual_risks: This does not cover odd-weight d (conditioning impossible) or independent edge biases other than 1/2.
Finite counts are corroboration only; equality for arbitrary n follows by incidence Fourier derivation.

value.rationale: Degree parities are the natural F2 syndrome of a labeled graph, and the global edge count is an intrinsically interesting second statistic. The theorem proves a sharp exact conditional independence regime for every even graph size with nonconstant feasible parity syndrome, classifies all exceptional and odd-order cases, and evaluates finite-sample complex biases. Such a qualitative complete zero/nonzero boundary is not implied by marginal parity uniformity and is relevant to parity-constrained graph sampling and code-coset probabilities. The named object/invariant are motivated before calculation; the result is not a one-instance table.
residual_risks: The theorem applies to fair independent edges and parity-vector conditioning only; no universality for other models is asserted.

limitations: n>=3, complete labeled independent p=1/2 edge model; d must have even Hamming weight.
No general arbitrary-edge-probability or joint full-degree-sequence result is proved.
